persons.name: Bora Özkent
persons.digest:
According to Bora Özkent last week was very rough: the **S&P 500** fell 1.82% on Friday, the **Nasdaq** 3.46%, the chip index 7.20%, and **Intel** had the biggest drop in its history (28.58%). He says the main cause is not earnings problems but hedge funds fleeing AI positions and closing leverage; lost search traffic at companies like **Reddit** and **Alphabet**, and negative free cash flow at **Amazon**, **Alphabet** and **Meta**, also spooked the market. He is keeping his AI-infrastructure thesis, says he is down more than 20% year to date, and thinks November–December seasonality could bring a rebound.

On the election he keeps his view that Democrats take the House and Republicans keep the Senate. There is a mildly positive tone in the Iran talks but no confirmation; if no deal comes today he assumes the war accelerates after the election. He cites about a 76% probability of a rate hike at the December Fed; this week he is watching **Apple**, **Palantir**, AMD, Arista, SMCI and ARM earnings plus ISM, JOLTS, ADP and Friday's jobs data.

items.title: Has the Nasdaq Found a Bottom?
items.summary: On Friday the S&P 500 fell 1.82%, the Nasdaq 3.46% and the chip index 7.20%; in October the chip index fell 15.36% and sits 26.96% below its peak. Because the VIX stayed below 20 there is no broad panic, and the equal-weight S&P 500 was positive until then. The damage is concentrated in semiconductors and AI: Intel fell 28.58% on PC weakness and other chip companies followed, though their cash flows are positive. He ties Reddit's 29.3% drop and Alphabet's 31.5% fall from its peak to search traffic shifting into AI; Amazon, Alphabet and Meta saw free cash flow turn negative. A Morgan Stanley report says hedge funds are fleeing AI positions at a record pace, and such pullbacks usually end in a new rally. He expects Democrats to take the House and Republicans the Senate; if no Iran deal comes today he assumes the war accelerates after the election. The probability of a December Fed hike is about 76%. This week brings Apple, Palantir, AMD, Arista, SMCI and ARM earnings plus ISM, JOLTS, ADP and Friday's jobs data. He stays in AI-infrastructure investments and says he is down more than 20% year to date.

assets.note: Biggest drop in its history (28.58%); PC weakness, while data center grew ~80%.
Down 29.3%; earnings weren't bad but no new users, Google no longer sends traffic.

assets.note: $21.9B of the $23.3B net loss is noncash.

items.title: Anthropic IPO valuation
items.summary: WSJ: large institutional investors are urging Anthropic toward a more conservative $1.5–1.6T valuation.

assets.note: Investors push for a $1.5–1.6T valuation.

items.title: Deutsche Bank upgrades CrowdStrike
items.summary: Deutsche Bank upgraded CrowdStrike to Buy, raising its target from $240 to $300.

assets.note: Target $300; market underestimates AI-driven cybersecurity demand.

items.title: Morgan Stanley downgrades Coinbase
items.summary: Coinbase cut to Underweight, target lowered from $258 to $120.

assets.note: Target $120; confidence in earnings recovery has deteriorated.

items.title: Prediction markets give Democrats 72% for the Senate
items.summary: Stocks seen winning under a Democratic Congress, such as solar and EVs, surged; per Morgan Stanley the S&P 500 has risen 6 and 12 months after every midterm since 1950.

persons.name: jrouldz
persons.digest: jrouldz highlighted hyperscalers' $2.5T revenue backlog and argued AI spending, unlike the fiber era, is supply constrained. He found **Oracle**'s backlog relative to market cap huge; he wrote his long-term account is down 18% from the July highs and that **Apple** has traded like a hedge in this environment.

items.title: Hyperscaler backlogs
items.summary: He wrote there are reports of massive revenue backlogs in AI-linked companies; hyperscalers' total backlog is $2.5T.

assets.note: Backlog is huge relative to market cap.

items.title: Why this isn't the fiber bubble
items.summary: He wrote that the fiber buildout was demand constrained and took 20 years to find demand, while AI is supply constrained.

items.title: -18% in long-term account
items.summary: He wrote his long-term account is down 18% from the July highs, with Apple, cybersecurity and biotech mitigating the pain.

assets.note: Among positions that cushioned the drop.

items.title: Apple doesn't spend on AI buildout
items.summary: He wrote Apple pays nothing for the AI buildout yet most people consume AI through Apple products.

assets.note: Trading like a hedge in this environment.

persons.name: cevikfinance
persons.digest: cevikfinance wrote that Morgan Stanley's tech momentum gauge fell deeper than even in the dotcom bust and that sectors like solar are being bought as Democrats lead the polls. He liked the **Tempus AI** and **Aehr** reports, noted **Marvell** fell after the **Lumentum** deal, and said Trump can launch limited strikes even if he loses Congress.

items.title: Tech momentum weaker than dotcom
items.summary: Morgan Stanley's tech, media and telecom momentum gauge is about 62% below its 12-month peak; even the dotcom bust did not show such a drop.

items.title: Trump can strike without Congress
items.summary: The US president can launch limited strikes without Congress; Iran could be attacked even if Republicans lose both chambers.

items.title: Democratic odds lifting solar
items.summary: He wrote that as Democrats lead polls, the market has begun buying sectors Trump dislikes, such as solar.

items.title: Tempus AI earnings
items.summary: He relayed Tempus revenue of $411.5M (+23%), adjusted EPS of $0.07 and a raised full-year guide.

assets.note: Good report; full-year guidance raised.

items.title: Marvell's drop
items.summary: He wrote MRVL fell because of the acquisition deal.

assets.note: Fell because of the deal.

holdings.name: SoFi Technologies
holdings.opinion: As the largest position at 18.8%, credit quality and funding costs are the main risk while rates stay high and risk aversion persists; single-stock concentration magnifies it.
ai_points: Position size amplifies single-stock risk.
Expected December rate hike could weigh on fintech multiples.
No company-specific negative development in today's sources.

holdings.name: Amundi MSCI Turkey (Acc)
holdings.opinion: The reserve sales and inflation outlook shared by Tunç Şatıroğlu call for caution on Turkey; the ETF's currency and macro risk need monitoring.
ai_points: According to Tunç Şatıroğlu inflation won't fall below 20% even by end-2027 (against).
Data relayed from Hakan Kara shows $24B of reserves sold since September (against).
At 12.9% the weight is reasonable and adds diversification (for).

holdings.name: Broadcom

mentions.quote: Examples like Nvidia, Micron, Broadcom, TSMC.
This move matters for $AVGO too.

holdings.why: According to Bora Özkent the chip selloff isn't earnings-driven and cash flows are positive; no new buy/sell trigger.
holdings.opinion: With the chip selloff ongoing the position is 12.9%; the Marvell–Lumentum merger could intensify competition in optical connectivity, which is the key thing to watch.
ai_points: Per Bora Özkent chip companies have no earnings problem (for).
The chip index fell 7.20% on Friday and volatility may persist (against).
Marvell–Lumentum could raise competition (against).

holdings.name: Meta Platforms A

mentions.quote: Amazon, Alphabet and Meta, all three big players, announced that their free cash flows turned negative.
Meta aims to issue at least $20B of bonds in dollars and euros to fund AI infrastructure and data-center expansion.

holdings.why: According to Bora Özkent Meta's free cash flow turned negative and it plans at least $20B of bonds; there is no clear level or date for a sale.
holdings.opinion: Negative cash flow and debt financing are what the market is punishing right now; payback on AI spending looks toward 2028.
ai_points: Per Bora Özkent hyperscalers' cash flow could be strong from 2028 (for).
Negative free cash flow and new bond issuance (against).
A 12.8% weight is reasonable but too early to add on this news flow (neutral).

holdings.name: BWX Technologies
holdings.why: In the Q3 relayed by wallstengine EPS beat and revenue missed; guidance of high-single-digit growth for 2027 isn't a sufficient trigger to buy or sell.
holdings.opinion: Nuclear demand and an $8.6B backlog are supportive; the small revenue miss and valuation are what to watch.
ai_points: Per wallstengine backlog is $8.6B (+16%) and free cash flow +59% (for).
Revenue missed and full-year revenue guidance is below estimates (against).

holdings.name: Reddit A

mentions.quote: The earnings weren't bad. But there are no new users.

holdings.why: According to Bora Özkent Reddit's 29.3% drop stems from a lack of new users; this is a risk observation rather than a sell level or date.
holdings.opinion: The shift of Google traffic to AI is the main risk to Reddit's user growth; a 9.4% weight may be high for this uncertainty.
ai_points: Per Bora Özkent the earnings weren't bad (for).
No new users and search traffic referrals dropped (against).
Rather than panic selling a stock that already fell hard, watch it (neutral).

holdings.name: Netflix
holdings.opinion: A defensive growth story outside the AI selloff; a 9.4% weight is reasonable, with advertising and content spending to watch.
ai_points: Not directly affected by the AI chip selloff (for).
No new company information in today's sources (neutral).

holdings.name: iShares USD Treasury Bond 20+yr EUR Hedged (Dist)

mentions.quote: We are approaching the December Fed. Rate-hike expectations are high there right now.
The Fed hiked in September for the first time since 2023, the market prices another hike in December, and the 10-year yield has topped 5% in recent months.

holdings.why: Bora Özkent says a December hike is expected; that is negative for long bonds but no concrete sell trigger (level/date) was shared.
holdings.opinion: Long-dated 20+ year bonds are the most sensitive to rate-hike expectations; the ISM prices index staying above 75 keeps the risk alive.
ai_points: Per Bora Özkent a December hike is expected (against).
If risk appetite deteriorates, bonds can act as a portfolio balancer (for).
Periods with the 10-year above 5% show the price risk (against).

holdings.name: FORGENT POWER SOLUTIONS INC.

mentions.quote: $FPS arttirildi.

holdings.why: Ahmet Sunelcan said he increased his position but gave no level or rationale.
holdings.opinion: The electrical-infrastructure theme is fed by AI power demand; a 5.3% weight is small but a recent IPO's volatility can be high.
ai_points: Ahmet Sunelcan increased his position (for).
As a recent IPO, volatility is high and news flow limited (against).
